I control this via my laptop and a program called 'Win2VNC' that moves *Only* my mouse/keyboard onto the TV. Normal VNC and RDC options don't work correctly, which is obvious to anyone who's used them. I don't want my HTPC screen on my laptop, I want my laptop keyboard and mouse on the HTPC screen.

Win2VNC has been my standard for a long time, easily more than a decade over my 2 prior generations of HTPC. Seems like most people who are in the same situation now use Synergy, so I've been beating my head against that for a few hours (using the older 1.4.x versions that are still available free). Searching around it looks like multiple other folks have the same problem connecting a linux pc to a Win 7 64-bit pc.

I'd consider switching the HTPC to linux but for Netflix. It's easily 90% of what we watch (which isn't a whole lot, Maybe 2 hours a day) because it's reliable, unlike Kodi streams.

Sorry, no smartphones or tablets, not really looking to buy an accessory (something else to sit around, need batteries, get lost/broken, etc...) I know I'm giving up other programs that are Windoze specific and MUST retain some sort of Windows OS to run them (my most used is a target trainer, RIKA, that was last updated to run on WinXP but my car OBDII software is Windows-only too ~ VCDS), I'll try them in wine/VM down the road.

I just need to control my HTPC from my laptop. Best if I can use something that allows my wife to continue to use Her laptop (Win8.1 with win2vnc) to control the HTPC too, but I'll teach her something new if it's as simple as win2vnc.

Thanks.
